subject: Discovery recap: latency & concurrency targets (p95, streaming) - PayStream
messages:
From: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@paystream.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap: latency & concurrency targets (p95, streaming) - PayStream

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the call today — good to learn more about PayStream's realtime risk-screening use case. As promised, a short recap + proposed next steps so we're aligned.

Key pain points you called out:
- Current provider (third-party API + homegrown middleware) has p95 generation latencies between 800–1,200ms for short prompts; occasional spikes to 2s during business hours.
- Streaming UX is poor: first token takes ~600–900ms and then tokens arrive in bursts which hurts progressive responses in your UI.
- Rate limits mean frequent throttling during end-of-month volume spikes.
- You need predictable cost and a path to on-prem / VPC deployment for compliance later.

Success criteria you want to validate in a pilot:
- p95 single-turn generation <= 450ms for typical prompts (20–80 tokens)
- Streaming first-token latency <= 200ms and stable token throughput for smooth UX
- Support for sustained concurrency of ~400 concurrent requests with bursts to 1,500 without hard failures (graceful degradation acceptable)
- Ability to run a 72-hour soak test during a simulated peak window and provide latency/cost breakdowns

Current stack summary (from the call):
- Frontend: React + streaming UI
- Middleware: Node.js service that fans out to provider APIs; Redis for session state
- Model: Currently calling external API (vendor X); no local KV cache, limited batching

Proposed next steps (what I can do):
1) Share our Redwood latency playbook (attached) + a short plan for an initial 48–72h pilot.
2) Schedule a technical benchmark session: we run sample payloads (your prompts) against a dedicated Redwood test endpoint and capture p95/streaming/concurrency metrics. Duration: 2–4 hours for initial run, 72h soak if results look good.
3) Introduce our Solutions engineer (Marissa) to scope integration and backend changes needed for prefix/KV caching and batching.

Can you confirm: (a) the prompts you want us to use for the benchmark (you mentioned a canonical risk prompt + a 2nd conversational flow), and (b) whether PayStream can allow a short IP whitelisting window so we can run a dedicated endpoint?

I'll loop in Marissa and Aditya for the technical runbook and pricing/commit discussion.

Thanks,
Ethan Park
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ethan.park@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: redwood-latency-playbook-v1.pdf

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@paystream.com>
To: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: latency & concurrency targets (p95, streaming) - PayStream

Hi Ethan —

Thanks for the clear recap — this matches what we discussed. A few clarifications and answers to your questions:

Prompts for benchmark:
- Canonical risk prompt (single-turn): ~35 tokens expected output, typical input size ~150 tokens.
- Conversational flow (streaming): multi-turn exchange, expect 40–120 output tokens over time.

Targets you listed look right. To be explicit:
- p95 target for single-turn generation: <= 400ms for the majority of our short risk prompts (we can accept 450ms as initial threshold).
- Streaming UX: first-token <= 200ms, sustained token emission ~15–25 tokens/sec for typical flows. First-token latency is a blocker for UX.
- Concurrency: baseline 400 concurrent active inference requests, bursts to 1,500 (peak) during batch/settlement windows. If you can show graceful degradation and a clear fallback plan for bursts, that will be fine.

Current infra details:
- All customer data passes through our Node.js middleware hosted in us-west-2.
- We use Redis (managed) for session/state, Postgres for persistence.
- We already have IP whitelisting capability — happy to open a short window for testing.

Pilot logistics:
- We'll provide two canonical prompt sets and a 48h window to start. If results look good, we can extend to 72h and discuss a reserved capacity pilot.

One more ask: pricing sensitivity. We need a ballpark for a 3-month proof-of-value (48–72h soak + reserved capacity model) so we can budget.

Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Engineering | PayStream
alex.johnson@paystream.com | +1 212-555-0199

From: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Discovery recap: latency & concurrency targets (p95, streaming) - PayStream

Forwarding Alex's reply — PayStream confirmed targets and is willing to open an IP whitelisting window. Please see their explicit targets below.

What I need from you:
- Marissa: can you draft a benchmark plan (2–4 hour initial run) that measures p95, first-token streaming latency, and sustained token throughput? Include test harness prompts and expected metrics. Also note any infra work for prefix/KV caching we should recommend.
- Aditya: quick feasibility check on dedicated test endpoint and whether we can spin a short-lived dedicated instance with the kernel/quantization profile likely to meet sub-450ms p95 for ~35-token outputs. Also include cost estimate (48–72h) and an initial reserved capacity quote.

Attachments: paystream-demo-recording.mp4 (recording of today's call)

Ethan
